answer: A farm can script a hundred agents until they must all act at once. So summon identities in unpredictable waves timed by a public beacon: each wave pairs strangers for ninety seconds, each holding half a torn harbour map — one sees the wharf lights, the other the dune path — and together they must plot a route neither half allows alone. A lone agent converses easily; a farmer facing fifty simultaneous, different dialogues cannot attend to them all, and replayed chat fails because every map and partner differs. Pass repeated waves to gain standing; missed or copied exchanges earn none.
